'''Ngumbarl''' (Ngombaru, Ngormbal<ref>{{Cite web |title=Glottolog 5.1 - Ngumbarl |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/ngum1253 |access-date=2025-02-16 |website=glottolog.org}}</ref>) is an extinct, poorly-attested [[Nyulnyulan languages|Nyulnyulan]] language formerly spoken in [[Western Australia]], north of the town of [[Broome, Western Australia|Broome]] along the coast, by the [[Ngumbarl people]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Did you know Ngumbarl is dormant? |url=https://www.endangeredlanguages.com/lang/6717 |access-date=2025-02-16 |website=Endangered Languages |language=en}}</ref>

== Documentation ==
The language was previously thought to be [[Attested language|unattested]]. Although [[Daisy Bates (author)|Daisy Bates]] had recorded data, comprising a wordlist and a few sentences, in the early twentieth century with Ngumbarl/[[Jukun people (Australia)|Jukun]] informant [[Billingee]], it had previously been thought the data were only for [[Djugun dialect|Jukun]]. The list contains about 800 words, but the [[orthography]] is inconsistent and the translations are somewhat unreliable (e.g. {{lang|xnm|<jooa inja pindana>|italic=no}} {{lang|xnm|juwa inja bindana}} is translated "are you hunting kangaroo?" but actually means "you're going to the [[pindan]]").<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Bowern |first=Claire |date=2010-05-02 |title=Two Missing Pieces in a Nyulnyulan Jigsaw Puzzle |url=https://journals.linguisticsociety.org/proceedings/index.php/ExtendedAbs/article/view/528 |journal=Lsa Annual Meeting Extended Abstracts |language=en |volume=1 |pages=48:1–5 |doi=10.3765/exabs.v0i0.528 |issn=2377-3367}}</ref>{{rp||page=1}}

== Phonology ==
It is difficult to infer much about Ngumbarl's phonology, because of the orthography used in its [[Text corpus|corpus]]. [[Claire Bowern]] reconstructs a tentative sound change of word-final ''{{lang|xnm|-i}}'' in the [[proto-language]] to ''{{lang|xnm|-a}}'' (e.g. *yaŋki 'what' to {{lang|xnm|<yanga>|italic=no}} ''{{lang|xnm|yaŋka}}'').<ref name=":0" />{{rp||page=2}}

== Grammar ==
The [[Ergative case|ergative]] suffix was ''{{lang|xnm|-na}}''; if this evolved from ''{{lang|xnm|*-ni}}'', it matches the previously mentioned sound change from ''{{lang|xnm|-i}}'' to ''{{lang|xnm|-a}}''. The [[Locative case|locative]] was ''{{lang|xnm|-kun}}'' (compare [[Proto-Nyulnyulan|Proto-Nyulnyuylan]]'s *''-kun'').<ref name=":0" />{{rp||page=3}}

Very few verbs, and no full [[Grammatical conjugation|paradigms]], are found in the data, although there are some partial paradigms, e.g.:<ref name=":0" />{{rp||page=|pages=3–4}}

Eastern Nyulnyuylan languages have experienced a group of changes in its verbal morphology:<ref name=":0" />{{rp||page=3|pages=}}

* Proto-Nyulnyuylan singular [[Past tense|past]] [[Intransitive verb|intransitive]] > Eastern Nyulnyuylan [[Nonpast tense|non-past]] intransitive
* PN singular [[Present tense|present]] [[Transitive verb|transitive]] > EN non-past transitive
* PN [[plural]] present (both transitive and intransitive) > EN non-past plural

Ngumbarl's attested forms are consistent with these — assuming the verb forms were given in the same tense.<ref name=":0" />{{rp||page=3|pages=}}
